value.rationale: Copeland score and uncoveredness are canonical but structurally different majority-tournament criteria. Separating the first tie-level difference from the first unique-winner difference isolates the smallest setting where an apparently decisive score winner remains nonexclusive under a stronger dominance-path criterion. The complete three-orbit first decisive layer gives a natural exact benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
